column3: cuVS shipping no GPU kd-tree is NOT the reason and must not be given as one. The reason is the structure: a kd-tree query is a per-query stack walk with data-dependent branching and per-lane divergent memory access, which is the shape a GPU is worst at, and above roughly 15 dimensions the pruning bound stops firing and it degenerates to a full scan -- so it would lose to the brute force in this directory on exactly the workloads it claims to help. THE THING A CALLER ASKING FOR A TREE ACTUALLY WANTS NOW EXISTS (2026-09-01): algorithm='rbc' on NearestNeighbors runs impl/neighbors/ball_cover/knn.mojo::rbc_knn_query, an EXACT k-NN over cuVS's RANDOM BALL COVER -- one level over sqrt(n) landmarks, no stack, no divergence, and the same index RadiusNeighbors already used. So this row is no longer 'we refuse the request'; it is 'we refuse the DATA STRUCTURE and serve the request with a better one'. What stays refused BY NAME is the two tree names, because naming them would describe the wrong algorithm. Gated by `pixi run check-ball-cover-knn`; DEVIATIONS 558-567 live in that file. GATE STATUS 2026-09-01, GREEN on Apple: the EXACTNESS arms pass; `check_rbc_knn_prune_is_load_bearing` had refused on the lattice fixture (sixteen rows at one exact distance, so a dropped neighbour is forgiven as a ZERO-ulp tie flip and that fixture could not witness the sabotage at any scale), the fixture was replaced with the tie-free scattered one plus a strictly-positive pruned-count precondition, and the confirming run LANDED the same day on both the FAST and IDENTICAL arms: PRUNED 25141 of 36864 candidate distances, BREAKS at prune_scale 0.95 on 1 of 96 rows. The PRUNING claim is verified on Apple M4 only; no second vendor has run it

Ours uses the plain two-sided triangle bound, which is exact, needs no division and no NaN repair, and halves the selector. column1: scikit-learn RadiusNeighbors / NearestNeighbors(algorithm='rbc') metric='cosine' / 'sqeuclidean' / minkowski p < 1
column3: and the refusal is now exactly as wide as its argument, which it was not before 2026-09-01. The ball cover's pruning IS the triangle inequality on the landmark radii, so the admitted set is THE METRICS: Euclidean (L2SqrtUnexpanded), L1/Manhattan, Linf/Chebyshev and Lp at p >= 1. What fails the inequality stays refused: `1 - cos` (three unit vectors at 0/60/120 degrees give 1.5 against 0.5 + 0.5, and d(x, 2x) = 0 breaks identity of indiscernibles), Lp at p < 1 (|x|^p is not subadditive; (0,0),(1,0),(1,1) at p = 1/2 gives 4 against 1 + 1) and SQUARED Euclidean (three collinear points at unit spacing give 4 against 1 + 1), which is BOTH expanded L2 tags. The expanded tags carry a second reason as well: DEVIATION 2 in ball_cover.mojo requires the build and the query to compute the compared quantities by the same formula, and the expanded identity loses the closest pair to cancellation
